paper.title: High-fidelity neutral atom gates leveraging low-rank Hessian optimization — Figure 2

model.name: 171Yb three-outcome state readout and single-qubit RB simulator
model.lattice: independent 171Yb qubits in the gate zone
model.boundary: finite-shot public observation; no privileged truth used by the fitted RB estimator

method.tool: cs-tweezer-sim public runtime and observation model
method.note: The simulator generates photon counts, classifications, retention/loss records, and RB successes. Camera counts use a published neutral-atom fluorescence calibration from Radnaev et al., not Liu's unavailable raw calibration. The RB decay uses the Liu raw-fidelity value as an explicit anchor and is therefore a closure demonstration, not an independent prediction.

params.name: shots per plotted point
params.source: standard simulation profile; paper does not publish a single common shot count
params.why: At an error near 4×10⁻³ this gives a binomial standard deviation near 2.8×10⁻⁴.
params.risk: Synthetic error bars may be smaller or larger than the paper because its exact sequence counts are unavailable.
params.fix: Compare fitted central values and quote our independently generated uncertainty.

params.name: readout outcomes
params.why: Postselection is meaningful only when loss remains a separate recorded outcome.
params.risk: Collapsing loss into a qubit state would inflate or obscure postselected fidelity.
params.fix: Preserve raw and no-loss analyses separately in input.in and plots.

params.name: readout calibration
params.source: simulator data package; different neutral-atom apparatus
params.why: Liu's raw photon distributions are unavailable, so this tests the full camera/threshold pipeline without fabricating their calibration.
params.risk: Confusion and loss probabilities need not match Liu Table I quantitatively.
params.fix: Report the differences as simulator predictions; keep the RB fidelity anchor separate.

actual.wall: completed locally in the simulator bridge run

risks: The exact experimental RB sequence list and raw photon records are unavailable.
The fluorescence calibration is from another apparatus; the single-qubit RB fidelity is a paper anchor rather than an independent prediction.

figures.plots: two-image photon counts and single-qubit randomized benchmarking
figures.x: first/second image photon counts or RB circuit depth
figures.y: assigned outcome density or success probability

observe.quantity: three-outcome confusion probabilities and raw/postselected RB decay
observe.normalization: probability per prepared state; success probability per RB depth
observe.states: prepared |0⟩ and |1⟩ with loss retained as a third outcome

figures.expected: The simulated Table-I closure should agree within generated sampling uncertainty; the RB fit should distinguish raw fidelity from the higher no-loss postselected fidelity and reproduce the paper's leakage-dominated trend.

results.why: The simulator reproduces the three-outcome camera/RB analysis pipeline, but the camera calibration comes from another apparatus and the RB fidelity is explicitly anchored to the paper.
results.wall: included in the simulator bridge run
changes: used the published Radnaev-2025 fluorescence fit because Liu raw photon calibration is unavailable
